- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral/negative.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model overcorrects downward; add 0.5–2% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.  
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3–7 days.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses 1–2 week mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 14-day moving average if sentiment is weak or mixed.
